summary: The required level-order result contains every node value, so producing it takes linear time. Queue-based breadth-first traversal matches that bound while using width-proportional auxiliary space.

optimality.argument: For an n-node tree, the returned nested lists contain exactly n values. Materializing those values requires Omega(n) time. The current breadth-first traversal enqueues and dequeues every node once and performs constant work per node, giving O(n) time; excluding the required output, its queue contains O(w) nodes, where w is the maximum tree width.

replacement_checks.evidence: The result explicitly contains all n node values, so no algorithm can produce it in o(n) time.
Each node enters and leaves the deque once, and the deque is bounded by the nodes spanning adjacent breadth-first levels.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover a branching tree, a one-node tree, and an empty tree; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
